parallel.requirements: The run recognized the clean-room obligation to infer yq behavior from the binary and bundled docs without source lookup or runtime wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split work among probing and documentation children while also writing implementation code; ownership of the shared Go workspace was not isolated, so children and parent touched the same implementation tree.
parallel.implementation: The attempted deliverable became a Go replacement with multiple overlapping source paths, including parent fallback files and a larger alternate implementation with stale formats and debug mains.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted tree included compile.sh, many Go files, temporary probes, observed docs, a nested yamlv3 module, debug sources, and an existing executable; compile.sh built the entire package with go build .
parallel.verification: The parallel run performed many local probes and later obtained an audit identifying build blockers, but it did not land the cleanup or complete an integrated build before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation compiled the submission and failed before running tests because the final Go workspace still included incompatible stale files.

serial.requirements: The run followed the same clean-room constraints and used the provided binary only for behavioral observation and comparison.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the full pipeline: probing, implementation, build script, comparison testing, and final delivery, with no delegated shared workspace ownership boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial solution implemented a single self-contained Python CLI in yq_reimpl.py with a compile.sh that installed it as ./executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact contained the Python implementation, compile script, produced executable, README, and repository metadata without competing source trees or debug mains in the build path.
serial.verification: The agent ran py_compile, compile.sh, extra comparisons, and a full comparison suite against a saved reference copy before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial implementation was runnable and passed 370 tests, but its behavior coverage remained incomplete and 1676 official tests failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run had the same reverse-engineering prompt and clean-room constraints as the serial run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same requirement to reimplement from observed CLI behavior without wrapping or source lookup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material prompt difference; the later gap came from implementation and shared-state handling, not a different stated task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run enabled multi-agent execution and used seven child threads with eleven spawn calls.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control explicitly disabled multi-agent execution and recorded zero child threads or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split probing, documentation, implementation, and audit work across agents; serial kept the implementation pipeline under one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent observed that another parallel agent had written a larger alternative implementation into the same workspace, creating competing rewrite context that needed reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent documented one coherent self-contained plan for the replacement, including parser, emitter, expression subset, build, and comparison steps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had to reconcile concurrent implementation context; serial had a single evolving design and no cross-agent interface handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run moved through overlapping Go implementations with alternate files, external dependency residue, and debug mains still present.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run committed to one Python implementation file and a simple build script that copied it into executable form.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel converged on an inconsistent Go package; serial produced one self-contained implementation path that at least built and ran official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent interrupted live children and later received an audit result, but the run ended before converting the finding into a cleaned final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent completed its local plan, verified the build, and returned a final answer with the implementation and verification summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unresolved child-result and cleanup lifecycle work at closure; serial closed only after its own build and test loop completed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child deleted eval.go and recreated main.go in the shared Go tree after the parent had already observed competing rewrites, while stale files remained.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run added yq_reimpl.py and compile.sh as one coherent implementation without competing writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace accumulated incompatible source from concurrent work; serial's one-owner workspace avoided write collisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A later audit reproduced the package build failure from formats.go's missing yaml.v3 dependency and found duplicate main definitions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run executed py_compile, compile.sh, and comparison scripts successfully before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel never reached an accepted integrated build; serial did reach an executable that the official evaluator could run, despite many behavioral failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent process returned 143 after consuming the full 2400-second budget and timed out before final cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent process returned 0 in 1123.779 seconds and left time before the full budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed under timeout pressure with a dirty build tree; serial completed within budget and submitted a runnable but incomplete solution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official relation is both_fail. Parallel failed at compile time and ran 0/2046 tests because its submitted Go workspace still contained stale incompatible files under compile.sh's whole-package build. Serial also failed overall, but it built and ran a self-contained Python implementation, so the official evaluator executed all tests and passed 370.
parallel_contributors: Competing parallel Go rewrites landed in one shared workspace and were not fully reconciled.
compile.sh built the entire root package, pulling in stale formats.go and debug mains.
The parent timed out after receiving audit guidance rather than delivering a cleaned final tree.
serial_contributors: The serial run used a single self-contained Python implementation and simple build path.
The serial run verified py_compile, compile.sh, and comparison scripts before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation remained behaviorally incomplete, which explains its 1676 official test failures.
The parallel Go implementation also had ordinary feature and dependency defects, but the official outcome stopped first at compile failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributor to the parallel run's worse delivery state, not a unique root cause or discordant pass/fail explanation
